title: Equine Parietal Bone Harvesting
author: Lilibeth A L.A.Z.M. Zambrano M
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xvkfn4w

steps.title: Remove soft tissue and organs
steps.instruction: In a room kept at 22 °C, use a scalpel to carefully remove all soft tissue from the bone, then excise the soft organs attached to the inner surface (brain, cerebellum, dura mater, etc.), and continuously irrigate the bone with saline solution.

steps.title: Mark sample area on bone
steps.instruction: With a pencil, draw a square on the parietal bone that covers at least one rectangular sample of 52 mm × 12 mm (accounting for saw thickness); adjust the rectangle size as needed for the number of samples and align the template according to the intended testing direction.

steps.title: Align skull and cut sample
steps.instruction: Place the skull so the vertical band saw is perpendicular to the drawn surface, then carefully cut the individual sample following the penciled pattern, allowing the saw to pass completely through the bone thickness, and permanently irrigate the cut bone with saline solution.

steps.title: Wrap and store samples
steps.instruction: Immediately wrap each harvested sample in gauze soaked with saline solution and store the wrapped samples at 4 °C.

steps.title: Harvest braincase section
steps.instruction: In a room at 22 °C and with at least two people present, carefully place the horse head in the vertical band saw, cut the section that encloses the braincase from the occipital bone to the beginning of the frontal bone, and permanently irrigate the cut bone with saline solution.
